about: Boomsma is a family distillery in Leeuwarden, the capital of Friesland in the far north of the Netherlands. Dirk Boomsma opened it in 1883 near the Oldehove, the city’s leaning church tower, and the fifth generation, Saskia and Chantoine Boomsma, run it today. From the start it has made genever, the Frisian herbal spirit Beerenburger and liqueurs, still from the original recipes.

Cloosterbitter traces its recipe to the 15th century and to Claerkamp, a Cistercian abbey founded around 1165 near Dokkum, a few kilometres north-east of Leeuwarden, and dissolved in 1580. Seventeen natural herbs form its base, among them gentian, nettle, dandelion, clover, angelica, mint and anise, with the rest kept a family secret. It is bottled at 40%.

Bright green, sweet and spicy, it is often described as a gentler, lower-proof cousin of green Chartreuse, and American bartenders have taken it up for that reason, using it in Last Words, Bijous and swizzles. Neat, it shows mint, anise and grassy herbs, a soft, rounded texture and a lightly bitter finish that makes it an easy introduction to Dutch herbal liqueurs.
facts: 17 herbs, including gentian, nettle, mint and anise
